plan.title: fix(swarm): the shipped subagent-heartbeat path is unarmed and a killed worker blocks its own resume

narratives.Description: fix(swarm): the shipped subagent-heartbeat path is unarmed and a killed worker blocks its own resume
narratives.Overview:
## Summary

The shipped subagent-heartbeat path (#1365 / #2824) is **unarmed by default**, a killed worker's delivery attempt never reaches a terminal state so resume is blocked, recovery is denied by a stale ritual, and uncommitted worker output is invisible to every gate.

Recut and **split** after a design critique (successor lean 5420886718) and an operator decision to carve the work. The original framing -- "Directive has no liveness signal" -- was refuted and is withdrawn; the mechanism exists and was never armed.

## Withdrawn

The filed version claimed no child-to-parent liveness channel exists. **False.** `docs/subagent-heartbeat.md`, `agent-prompt-preamble.md:538-550`, `task agent:monitor`, `task verify:subagent-alive`, `REDISPATCH_OK`, and swarm Phase 4 all ship. The overnight cohort simply had no `.deft-scratch/subagent-status/` directory in any of its seven worktrees, because the dispatch envelopes never created one.

Three of the four original suggestions are also withdrawn: last-seen on the C2 manifest (written `mode: "replace"`, erased next launch), a child-written death event (the child is dead), and treating this as an occupancy-lease dimension.

## Split out of this issue

- **#3777** -- operator re-entry visibility without a live parent. The genuinely unserved need, with no design and every obvious artifact ruled out. Needs its own critique arc.
- **#3778** -- reconciling the two existing classifiers, which disagree about what a missing heartbeat record means. A decision, not an implementation.

What remains here is four pieces of ordinary engineering.

## 1. Arm the shipped path

Dispatch envelopes do not create the scratch directory, do not instruct workers to heartbeat, and do not set `--require-agent`. Until they do, `verify:subagent-alive` returns a configuration error rather than a verdict, and a host-kill is indistinguishable from "never started."

This is the single most actionable line in the original issue, and it is a defect in the dispatch path rather than in the heartbeat mechanism.

## 2. A killed worker's attempt must reach a terminal state

Swarm pre-dispatch wires `DENY_DUPLICATE_ACTIVE` with `maxActiveAttempts: 1`, and `completeAttempt` is caller-driven. Measured: **79 of 100 on-disk delivery-attempt ledgers were still `queued` or `running`**, none moved on 08-24 or 08-25.

So a killed worker sits `running` forever, `REDISPATCH_OK` and `DENY_DUPLICATE_ACTIVE` contradict each other, and resume is blocked until a human cancels. Takeover must be documented as `swarm:pre-dispatch --action cancel` followed by begin.

## 3. Recovery must survive a stale ritual

Observed on a second disconnect at 01:22 on 2026-08-26. A parent that detects a dead child and tries to re-dispatch is **denied by the gated session ritual** if the cohort has run past the four-hour staleness window. Re-arming then reclaims the occupancy lease, which under the identity defect blocks the parent's own direct writes until released.

So recovery from a dead child currently walks through two other open defects. Either the recovery dispatch re-arms as part of its own flow, or the denial names `session:start --rearm` instead of failing bare.

## 4. Instruct workers to commit early

The 01:22 disconnect killed a worker with **0 commits and 10 dirty paths** -- roughly 18 KB of complete, correct source and tests existing only as uncommitted worktree state. Invisible to `verify:orphan-active`, invisible to the ledger, recoverable only because someone read the directory.

## What stands from the original filing

- **The environmental claims.** Four clusters in one night, clean Windows event log, no vendor incident, deaths correlating by wall-clock rather than by last tool call. Unchallenged. A fifth instance occurred on 2026-08-26, bringing observed deaths to eleven.
- **Residue**, with a correction: `verify:orphan-active` only fails active or running briefs whose issues are closed or PRs merged, so it could never have seen the worker that died before opening a PR. It is not a liveness surface.
- **213 registered worktrees**, not "over 150" as filed.

## Scope

**Related to #3613, not a child of it.** This tracker's shape is the worktree occupancy lease -- a session signalling about *itself*. Child mortality is a parent observing *another process*, already owned by #1365 / #2824 / #3228. The causal link runs the other way: a killed worker skips `releaseOccupancy`, so every disconnect mints ghost leases, making this an **upstream producer of #3604**.

## Acceptance

- [ ] Dispatch envelopes arm the shipped path: parent creates the scratch directory, worker is instructed to heartbeat, `--require-agent` is set
- [ ] A killed worker's delivery attempt reaches a terminal state so `DENY_DUPLICATE_ACTIVE` stops blocking resume; takeover documented as cancel-then-begin
- [ ] A recovery dispatch after a disconnect is not blocked by a stale ritual, or the denial names the re-arm verb
- [ ] Dispatch envelopes instruct workers to commit early
- [ ] CHANGELOG `[Unreleased]` entry

## Out of scope

- Operator re-entry without a live parent -- **#3777**
- Reconciling the two classifiers -- **#3778**. Do not add a third classifier here.
- A new cohort last-seen artifact or `DEAD` chip -- rejected; duplicates shipped surfaces and dies on manifest replace.
- Occupancy lease semantics (#3599, #3729, #3755) and worktree accumulation (#3604).

## Related

#3777, #3778, #1365, #2824, #3228, #3143, #3604, #3613 (related, not parent), #3742.

## Triage

mechanism-shaped: true

design-critique: warranted, because the issue deliberately stops short of a design ("Suggestions (not a design)") while the thing it gestures at — a parent-observable liveness signal for dispatched children — would sit on every swarm and solo-worker dispatch path in the framework. An always-on coordination channel between parent and child is a mechanism, and its failure modes (false alive, false dead, per-turn cost, which side writes the signal) are not settled by the body.

refutation-target: Directive has no liveness signal from a dispatched child back to its orchestrator, so a new parent-side mechanism is required.

## What the triage author is asserting

Three claims carry the issue.

1. **Host disconnects are environmental and will recur.** Well supported: four clusters in one night, a clean Windows event log across the window, no vendor incident, and deaths that correlate by wall-clock rather than by last tool call.
2. **Nothing lets a parent observe that its children stopped existing.** Asserted from absence. The body does not survey what already exists — the delivery-attempt ledger (#3143), dual stop (#2442), `verify:orphan-active`, or whatever the host itself exposes about a spawned agent — and rule each out as a liveness surface.
3. **The residue is downstream of the same cause.** A killed worker cannot run its release path, so every disconnect mints ghost leases (#3604) and orphaned briefs.

Claim 2 is load-bearing and is the one argued from absence rather than inspection. That is the refutation target.

## Scope note

Filed under #3613 as a fourth dimension — child mortality — alongside liveness (#3599), lifecycle (#3604), and keyspace (#3607). Whether it belongs in that frame is itself open. The three lease dimensions all concern a session signalling about *itself*; this one concerns a parent observing *another process*, which may be a different problem wearing the same clothes.

## Thread repair — my comments posted as literal file paths

Every parent comment I posted to this arc before this one landed as the single literal string `@C:\Users\msada\AppData\Local\Temp\...`, not as its content. Cause: I used `gh api ... -f body=@<file>`. The `-f` / `--raw-field` flag posts a string literal and performs no `@` file expansion; that is `-F` / `--field`, or the form this repository's own guidance specifies, `gh issue comment <N> --body-file <path>`. I verified the correct form against a scratch comment before repairing.

All affected comments have been reposted with their real content and the stubs deleted. Thirteen stubs in total across this cluster.

## Consequence for the critics already dispatched

The critics on this arc were dispatched with an id ceiling pointing at one of those stubs, so **the thread carried them nothing** — the Stop 1 write-back, the charter and spend record, and the reopening corrections were all unreadable at the ceiling.

Their critiques are still valid, because the dispatch envelope carried that content directly: the refutation target where the charter was refutation, the withdrawn claims where there were withdrawals, the SHA, the round, and the audit targets. What they lost was the ability to read it a second time in the thread. One critic noticed and reported it as a finding, which is the correct behaviour and is now on the record twice over.

I am not re-running any critic that already posted. Re-dispatching for a defect in the parent's plumbing would spend a retry slot on nothing, and the contract reserves reiteration for residual disagreement.

## My own dispatch instruction was the propagation vector

The envelope I sent each critic told it to post using `gh api ... -f body=@<path>`. That instruction was wrong, and one critic followed it faithfully — its comment posted as a path stub. Its findings were recovered verbatim from its output file and posted unmodified, with provenance disclosed on that comment. Later dispatches in this cluster use `--body-file`.

Recording this as a parent process defect rather than quietly fixing it: a parent that hands workers a broken command turns one mistake into N.

### Comment by @MScottAdams (2026-08-26T04:56:46Z)

model: claude-opus-5-thinking-high-fast

## Findings

### Parent-observable liveness already shipped — `sharpens-framing`

**Evidence:** `docs/subagent-heartbeat.md` (#1365, Cursor false-alive § #2824); `packages/cli/src/verify-subagent-alive.ts:4-35` (fail-closed gate, default 30 min threshold, exit 1 prints `REDISPATCH_OK`); `content/skills/deft-directive-swarm/references/core-phase-4.md:14-23` (Phase 4 MUST run `task agent:monitor` every ~2-3 min alongside worktree git checks); `content/commands.md:327` (worker liveness pointer). Completed xBRIEF for #2824 exists under `xbrief/completed/`.

**Failure mode:** The issue's load-bearing claim — "Directive has no liveness signal from a dispatched child back to its orchestrator" — binds as a greenfield mechanism gap. That misroutes triage toward inventing a new parent-child channel when a filesystem heartbeat contract, monitor verb, and REDISPATCH_OK gate are already normative and shipped.

**Disposition consequence:** The lean cannot bind on "nothing exists." Reframe the gap as **operational** (parent did not arm Phase 4 monitoring / workers did not write heartbeats / `#2824` wiring incomplete for this cohort) or **semantic** (instant host-kill vs stale-heartbeat — see next finding). Any build should extend or enforce the existing contract, not assume absence.

---

### Heartbeat detects staleness, not instant host-kill — `sharpens-framing`

**Evidence:** `packages/core/src/orchestration/subagent-monitor.ts:11` (`DEFAULT_THRESHOLD_MINUTES = 30`); `packages/core/src/orchestration/subagent-monitor.ts:191-193` (STALE only when `age_seconds > thresholdSeconds` and `terminal_state` is null). Workspace disconnect kills mid-turn without a terminal heartbeat write; the last on-disk record can remain fresh for up to the threshold. Measured: default threshold is 30 minutes (not sub-minute). Grep for `turn_ended` / `Workspace Disconnected` across the repo at dispatch SHA: **zero matches** (unverified whether host exposes this outside the repo).

**Failure mode:** Four workers dying in one host event can leave four OK heartbeat records. `task verify:subagent-alive` exits 0 until records age out or go missing — the inverse of #2824 false-alive (host says running + stale heartbeat), but equally silent to the parent if the monitor loop is not running or threshold is too coarse.

**Disposition consequence:** Scope the problem to **instant correlated mortality** and **host-bridge failure**, not generic "no liveness." A design must either tighten the monitor threshold for Cursor cohorts, add host-transcript / platform lifecycle as a supplementary kill signal (see `docs/subagent-heartbeat.md:139-143` MAY), or accept that file-heartbeat alone cannot detect sub-threshold death.

---

### Seven-hour silence implicates parent monitor cessation — `sharpens-framing`

**Evidence:** Issue body (four correlated death clusters, then ~7h operator silence until 09:22). `content/skills/deft-directive-swarm/references/core-phase-4.md:23` (monitor MUST poll every ~2-3 min). `content/skills/deft-directive-swarm/references/core-phase-5-6.md:33` (`FAILED` / silent → `task verify:subagent-alive`, exit 1 → `REDISPATCH_OK`). `packages/core/src/swarm/launch.ts:865-898` — `buildManifest` persists dispatch-time fields only; no runtime last-seen (grep `launch.ts` for `subagent-status` / heartbeat mkdir: **no matches** at dispatch SHA).

**Failure mode:** If Phase 4 monitoring were armed and heartbeats present, STALE/missing records should surface within one monitor iteration (minutes), not hours. Seven-hour silence is consistent with (a) the parent conversation itself disrupted by the same workspace bridge drop, (b) workers never writing heartbeats (contract violation), or (c) monitor loop never started — not with a missing mechanism type alone.

**Disposition consequence:** Separate **child death** from **parent observability loop death**. Remediation split: resume/re-arm parent monitor after host reconnect; audit worktree `.deft-scratch/subagent-status/` for the killed cohort before designing new artifacts.

---

### Downstream gates are residue detectors, not liveness — `footnote`

**Evidence:** `packages/core/src/orphan-active/evaluate.ts:1-34` (scans `xbrief/active/` vs GitHub issue/PR state; no agent/process probe). `packages/core/src/delivery-attempt/evaluate.ts:1-6` (pre-dispatch circuit breaker; durable retry budget, not poll loop). Issue-cited `verify:orphan-active` exit 201 at filing: **unverified at dispatch SHA** (measured now at HEAD=c784755: exit 0, 0 active briefs — residue may have been cleaned post-incident).

**Failure mode:** Listing these under "nothing lets a parent observe children stopped" overstates their role. They catch ghost leases and WIP consumption after the fact; they cannot prevent seven-hour silent cohorts.

**Disposition consequence:** Keep the residue section as downstream impact evidence; do not treat it as proof of a missing liveness layer.

---

### #3613 "fourth dimension" conflates lease self-signal with child observability — `sharpens-framing`

**Evidence:** Issue § Relation to #3613. `packages/core/src/session/occupancy.ts:28-49` (session claims `.deft/occupancy.json`, 20 min heartbeat TTL — occupant signals about *itself*). `docs/subagent-heartbeat.md:157-180` (child writes `.deft-scratch/subagent-status/<agent-id>.json`; parent reads across worktrees — cross-process observability, landed under #1365/#2824).

**Failure mode:** Labeling this "child mortality" as a fourth occupancy-lease dimension implies the #3613 tracker owns a problem whose shipped surface lives in swarm Phase 4 + subagent heartbeat, not occupancy keyspace/lifecycle. Risk of duplicate tracking and wrong remediation owner (lease reap vs monitor wiring).

**Disposition consequence:** Cross-link #2824/#1365 explicitly; justify #3613 placement or file as a sibling host-reliability item under swarm/orchestration rather than extending the lease model.

---

### "Cohort manifest with last-seen" duplicates static launch manifest — `sharpens-framing`

**Evidence:** `packages/core/src/swarm/launch.ts:675,1207-1218` (persists `.deft/swarm-launch-manifest.json`); `packages/core/src/swarm/launch.ts:865-898` (per-child `story_id`, `worktree_path`, `branch`, routing metadata — no `agent_id`, no `last_seen`, no liveness). Measured: `git worktree list | Measure-Object -Line` → **213** worktrees at dispatch SHA (issue cited 150+ at filing — consistent accumulation, unverified causal link).

**Failure mode:** The first suggestion reads like a new artifact when a cohort manifest already exists but is dispatch-frozen. A second manifest type increases drift risk unless one file becomes the runtime-augmented source of truth.

**Disposition consequence:** Prefer extending launch manifest or aggregating per-worktree heartbeat sweeps (`task agent:monitor --scratch-dir <wt>/.deft-scratch/subagent-status` per `core-phase-4.md:18-20`) over a parallel "last-seen manifest."

---

## Injection / swarm lens

This target changes **concurrency**, **worktrees**, and **shared cohort state** — lens applies. The failure is a correlated host event killing N background Cursor `Task` workers on N worktrees while the parent loses its monitor loop. Existing controls are filesystem heartbeats (child→parent via gitignored scratch), Phase 4 polling (parent obligation), REDISPATCH_OK (takeover authorization), dual stop on repair loops (#2442), and downstream orphan gates — but none form a **deterministic** closed loop for workspace-bridge disconnect without (1) parent survival, (2) heartbeat writes, and (3) sub-threshold death detection. No repo-native handler for host `turn_ended` / workspace-disconnect events (grep: zero). Host "still running" false-alive is documented (#2824); **fresh-heartbeat / dead-process** false-alive is not.

## Road not taken

Wire and tighten **existing** `#2824`/`#1365` surfaces first: parent `mkdir` scratch dirs at dispatch, mandate heartbeats in worker envelopes, run `task verify:subagent-alive --require-agent <id> --threshold-minutes 5` on the Phase 4 cadence, and treat missing terminal heartbeat + host transcript error as `REDISPATCH_OK` — rather than a new cohort liveness channel.

## Steelman

The incident is real and well-evidenced: correlated wall-clock death clusters, clean Windows event log, ten killed workers, orphan briefs and worktree residue at filing. Even with shipped prose, **this cohort experienced the #1166 recurrence class** — contract on paper did not prevent operator-visible silence. A critic who stops at "already exists" without naming the instant-kill blind spot and parent-loop cessation would under-read the blast radius. The issue's residue and environmental claims (claims 1 and 3) stand; only claim 2 overgeneralizes from absence without inventory.


### Comment by @MScottAdams (2026-08-26T04:57:49Z)

model: gpt-5.6-sol-medium
role: critic

## Existing detector, missing enforcement
class: blocks-the-design

Evidence: the repository already requires every long-running Cursor Task worker to emit a heartbeat and already defines missing or stale heartbeat as `REDISPATCH_OK` (`docs/subagent-heartbeat.md:19-31`, `docs/subagent-heartbeat.md:38-62`). The executable gate resolves required agent ids against heartbeat records and exits stale when a required record is absent or unhealthy (`packages/cli/src/verify-subagent-alive.ts:136-157`, `packages/cli/src/verify-subagent-alive.ts:193-210`); it is exposed as `task verify:subagent-alive` (`tasks/verify.yml:619-627`). The worker preamble also tells parents to create the status directory, observe startup grace, and invoke the gate each poll iteration (`content/templates/agent-prompt-preamble.md:534-557`).

Measured at `c784755f08773b8e861567d8df7780aea310cc57`: `git worktree list --porcelain` reports 213 registered worktrees, while recursive enumeration under `.deft-scratch/worktrees` found zero heartbeat JSON records and zero delivery-attempt ledger JSON records. The surviving `b3721` worktree has three commits on `fix/3721-literal-ac-prose`, including a pushed tracking branch, but no heartbeat directory. This is evidence of non-adoption or missing spawn wiring, not absence of a designed signal.

Concrete failure mode: accepting the issue's greenfield premise can add a second liveness representation while leaving the actual recurrence intact: workers are dispatched without establishing the already-required record, and the parent never invokes the already-shipped fail-closed gate.

Disposition consequence: the issue cannot bind as “Directive has no liveness signal” or as a request for a new heartbeat concept. Reframe it as deterministic spawn registration plus enforcement of the existing heartbeat/takeover contract, and audit why the affected Cursor dispatches had neither heartbeat files nor delivery-attempt rows.

## Watcher shares the failed workspace
class: blocks-the-design

Evidence: `task swarm:launch` persists dispatch-preparation records and returns; its manifest entries contain story, xBRIEF, worktree, branch, allocation, occupancy, routing, and auth data, but no spawned `agent_id`, attempt id, or liveness owner (`packages/core/src/swarm/launch.ts:821-900`, `packages/core/src/swarm/launch.ts:1187-1255`). The swarm contract explicitly says the manifest is prep and the host adapter performs the spawn (`content/skills/deft-directive-swarm/references/core-phase-3.md:14-20`). Detection is then a parent-driven pull at each monitor iteration (`content/skills/deft-directive-swarm/references/core-phase-4.md:10-29`).

Concrete failure mode: if the workspace bridge event suspends or kills the parent monitor along with its children, heartbeat files can become stale but no in-workspace actor executes the sweep or reports it. The issue's seven-hour silent interval is consistent with this shared-fault-domain failure; whether the parent process itself remained runnable through each bridge drop is unverified.

Disposition consequence: state the service objective before selecting a mechanism. If the objective is detection on parent re-entry, the existing file heartbeat plus a durable spawn registry is sufficient. If it is an operator-visible alert while the whole workspace is disconnected, an in-band parent query cannot satisfy it; the watcher or host lifecycle callback must live outside that workspace failure domain.

Road not taken: another per-child `last-seen` field inside the same workspace. Steelman: it gives a compact cohort view when only a child dies. It does not survive loss of the only reader. Evidence that the parent remains active and callable during this exact disconnect class would flip this verdict.

## Recovery must fence the old attempt
class: sharpens-framing

Evidence: the delivery-attempt model already has durable `running` state plus `workerId` and `externalRunId` (`packages/core/src/delivery-attempt/types.ts:99-116`), but “active” is only a status predicate; it has no age or heartbeat test (`packages/core/src/delivery-attempt/ledger.ts:605-610`). A running row therefore makes the pre-dispatch gate return `DENY_DUPLICATE_ACTIVE` indefinitely (`packages/core/src/delivery-attempt/evaluate.ts:161-176`). The existing takeover path is explicit cancel-then-begin, never concurrent replacement (`packages/core/src/swarm/pre-dispatch.ts:334-380`, `content/skills/deft-directive-swarm/references/core-phase-4.md:132-155`).

Concrete failure mode: independently expiring a manifest lease or heartbeat and spawning a replacement leaves the old delivery attempt active, so the gate either blocks recovery or gets bypassed. Conversely, automatically cancelling on one stale timestamp can create two writers if the old worker resumes after a delayed heartbeat.

Disposition consequence: define one fenced transition from `(cohort, story, attempt, host-run)` to terminal-dead/cancelled before replacement. Reuse the delivery-attempt key and cancel-then-begin semantics; do not create an unrelated expiring “parent holds child” lease. Resume-versus-replace is host capability, while worktree recovery is a separate decision.

## Occupancy is consequence, not owner
class: sharpens-framing

Evidence: occupancy represents one session holding one worktree, with its own session id and 20-minute heartbeat TTL (`packages/core/src/session/occupancy.ts:26-45`, `packages/core/src/session/occupancy.ts:137-169`). Worker liveness instead identifies a child and parent and classifies the child's execution phase (`packages/core/src/orchestration/subagent-monitor.ts:24-45`, `packages/core/src/orchestration/subagent-monitor.ts:150-193`). The launch manifest carries the cohort's occupancy session id, not child execution identities (`packages/core/src/swarm/launch.ts:865-898`).

Measured tracker state: REST inspection of #3613 found three comments and no canonical `## Current shape (as of pass-N)` comment, so the tracker body's “mortality dimension” placement is not a current-shape decision.

Concrete failure mode: making child mortality another occupancy dimension conflates two owners and clocks. A worker can die while the parent session and its occupancy remain valid; a parent can die while a worker or external run remains recoverable. One TTL cannot safely answer both.

Disposition consequence: keep #3730 causally related to #3604 because dead workers produce cleanup residue, but place the corrective contract under swarm worker supervision / delivery attempts. Occupancy should consume terminal cohort cleanup outcomes; it should not own child liveness.

Swarm/authority note: heartbeat records are worker-written shared state. The current required-agent gate selects by `agent_id` and does not bind an expected `parent_id`, cohort id, attempt id, or dispatch timestamp (`packages/cli/src/verify-subagent-alive.ts:136-151`). Any durable registry added here must bind those identities and reject pre-dispatch or cross-cohort records; otherwise stale residue can produce false-alive or false-dead decisions.

## Existing liveness path unused

`blocks-the-design`

**Evidence:** Directive already has a child→parent liveness channel. Long-running Cursor `Task` implement leaves must write `.deft-scratch/subagent-status/<agent-id>.json` (`docs/subagent-heartbeat.md:19-26`, `:157-171`; preamble `content/templates/agent-prompt-preamble.md:538-550`). The parent asks "are my children alive" with `task agent:monitor` / `task verify:subagent-alive` (`docs/subagent-heartbeat.md:38-61`; `packages/cli/src/verify-subagent-alive.ts:20-35`). Stale or missing heartbeats print `REDISPATCH_OK` and authorize takeover (`docs/subagent-heartbeat.md:45-50`; `host-cursor.md:31`). Phase 4 already names this the canonical alive-check (`content/skills/deft-directive-swarm/references/core-phase-4.md:14-23`). The overnight worktrees have no status directory at all. The body never surveys this surface.

**Failure mode:** Binding "a new parent-side mechanism is required because nothing exists" mints a second liveness channel while the first was not written, not mkdir'd, and not polled. Two surfaces that both depend on adoption will fail the same way.

**Disposition:** Do not bind a greenfield last-seen / death-state design from the absence claim. Restate the lean as: the #1365 / #2824 path was not in use on this cohort, and the remaining holes below are what still need a contract. Related: #2824, #1365, #2879.

## Shared-bridge observer

`sharpens-framing`

**Evidence:** The kill event is a Cursor workspace-bridge drop. Host-cursor treats the parent and the `Task` leaves as one workspace (`content/skills/deft-directive-swarm/references/host-cursor.md:13-17`: parent notified on completion). A file heartbeat can survive the drop; a parent on the same bridge cannot read it while the bridge is down. The 7h silence is operator-re-entry latency, not a proof that no queryable signal can exist.

**Failure mode:** Designing an always-on parent↔child channel assumes a live parent. On this host, the observer dies with the observed. A "parent can ask" verb does not page anyone at 02:29.

**Disposition:** Split the lean into (a) in-flight observation while some process on that workspace is still up, and (b) morning-after operator visibility that must not require a live parent. Do not treat (b) as a missing child→parent socket.

## Occupancy tracker misfit

`sharpens-framing`

**Evidence:** #3613's common shape is gaps in the *worktree occupancy lease* (self-signal: who may mutate this tree). Occupancy TTL is 20 minutes and join protocols are `none` | `heartbeat-file` | `parent-message` (`packages/core/src/session/occupancy.ts:28-32`). Default join is `none`. Child mortality is parent-observes-another-process, already owned by #1365's per-worktree status files — a different primitive and keyspace. Causal link to #3604 is real (dead workers skip `releaseOccupancy`); that makes this an upstream producer, not a fourth lease dimension.

**Failure mode:** Keeping #3730 as #3613 "Mortality" biases the next build toward `occupancy.json` last-seen. That file is per-tree write-exclusion, expire-to-free, and session-self. It will not give a parent a cohort roster, and it collides with #3599 (frozen self-heartbeat) and #3729 (fail-open when expired).

**Disposition:** Related-to #3604 / #3613. Do not bind it as a lease-model dimension. If a tracker is needed, it is swarm/host-adapter topology, next to #1365 / #2824 / #3228.

## Child-write death hole

`sharpens-framing`

**Evidence:** Heartbeats are child-written, every 2–3 minutes, with a required terminal write before exit (`docs/subagent-heartbeat.md:259-279`). A workspace disconnect mid-tool cannot write `terminal_state`. Phase 4 still says to treat a missing record as "alive but quiet" on the Grok Build path (`core-phase-4.md:29`), while #2824 / `verify:subagent-alive` treat missing *required* agents as dead — but only after the parent mkdir'd the scratch dir (`docs/subagent-heartbeat.md:100-123`). Measured: the b3721 probe exits 2 (config), not 1 (`REDISPATCH_OK`).

**Failure mode:** Host-kill looks like "never started" to the gate that would authorize takeover. Silence is not a distinct `DEAD` token; it is STALE, missing, or config-error depending on whether the parent prepared the dir.

**Disposition:** If anything new is warranted, it is not a child-written death event (the child is dead). It is a mechanical parent/operator inference from STALE-or-missing *after* mkdir, plus host transcript `turn_ended` when readable. Reconcile Phase 4 `:29` with #2824 before adding a third classifier.

## Resume gate treats death as live

`sharpens-framing`

**Evidence:** Swarm pre-dispatch wires #3143 `DENY_DUPLICATE_ACTIVE` (`maxActiveAttempts: 1`) so a non-terminal attempt blocks spawn (`packages/core/src/swarm/pre-dispatch.ts:1-9`; `packages/core/src/delivery-attempt/types.ts:194-195`; `core-phase-4.md:132-156`). The deny hint is "resume the live leaf, or takeover = cancel then begin" (`pre-dispatch.ts:463-466`). `completeAttempt` is caller-driven (`packages/core/src/delivery-attempt/ledger.ts:676-678`). 79 of 100 on-disk units are still `queued`/`running`; none moved on 08-24/25, so this cohort did not close attempts either.

**Failure mode:** "No resume" is not only missing death detection. A killed worker left `running` is classified as a live peer. `REDISPATCH_OK` and `DENY_DUPLICATE_ACTIVE` fight until someone cancels.

**Disposition:** Any mortality lean must name takeover = `swarm:pre-dispatch --action cancel` then begin (`core-phase-4.md:147-149`). Do not add a death status that is not a `complete` / `cancel` input.

## Manifest last-seen is PREP overwrite

`sharpens-framing`

**Evidence:** The C2 launch manifest is static dispatch PREP: `story_id`, paths, `allocation_context`, `occupancy_session_id` (`packages/core/src/swarm/launch.ts:865-874`). `swarm:launch` writes it with `mode: "replace"` (`launch.ts:1213-1218`). Measured: the file now holds 3596, not the overnight seven. There is no `last_seen` field in `buildManifest`.

**Failure mode:** Putting runtime last-seen on that file dies at the next launch. It also mixes consent/allocation with liveness.

**Disposition:** Reject last-seen-on-manifest. If a durable cohort roster is needed, it is a different artifact than C2 PREP. The existing per-worktree heartbeat files already are that roster when written.

## False-dead duplicate-agent

`sharpens-framing`

**Evidence (injection / swarm lens):** The target changes concurrency, worktrees, shared state, identity, and envelopes. Phase 4 Duplicate-Agent Failure Mode (`core-phase-4.md:171-178`): a false-dead call plus a replacement spawn puts two writers on one worktree. `REDISPATCH_OK` is the existing authorization token (`verify-subagent-alive.ts:203-204`). Host transcript strings are untrusted input. Occupancy `session_id`, heartbeat `agent_id`, and ledger `workerId` are three identities.

**Failure mode:** A new "children died" signal that is cheaper to fire than #2824's mkdir + grace + `--require-agent` will re-open #261 / #263 on every workspace blip. Four clustered deaths make a batch re-dispatch especially tempting.

**Disposition:** Who may declare dead, after what grace, and which id is cancelled, must be deterministic. Do not add a parallel death bit. Untrusted host error text is evidence for a probe, not a spawn license.

## orphan-active is shipped residue

`footnote`

`verify:orphan-active` only fails active/running briefs whose issues are closed or PRs merged (`packages/core/src/orphan-active/evaluate.ts:90-91, :307-310`). It cannot see #3721 (open, no PR). The body's two hits were downstream #2321 residue, now in `completed/`. Not a liveness surface.

## Dual stop and parent-hang are not mortality

`footnote`

#2442 is a loop budget (`main.md:113-140`; Phase 4 monitor envelope `:63-75`). #3131 / `evaluateParentTurnShape` is a live parent repeating text while children may be healthy. #3143 is a pre-dispatch circuit breaker, not a heartbeat. None of these observe host-kill. Dual stop cannot fire if the monitor died on the same bridge.

## Road-not-taken

Chose: treat #1365 / #2824 / #3228 as the liveness + takeover stack; reframe this issue as adoption, same-bridge observer, and operator re-entry. Rejected: a new cohort last-seen / `DEAD` chip as the primary design.

## Steelman

Strongest rejected lean: child-written heartbeats cannot record a mid-tool host kill, and a same-bridge parent cannot poll, so something *mechanical and off-bridge* (or morning-after without child writes) is still required. That would flip this critic if the next lean is "operator re-entry probe that does not depend on the child having written, and does not sit on C2 PREP / occupancy.json" — not if it is "Directive has no liveness signal."

## Successor lean — round 1, N=3 panel complete

Panel: `claude-opus-5-thinking-high-fast` (5420796899), `gpt-5.6-sol-medium` (5420803777), `cursor-grok-4.6-high-fast` (5420818543). Three of three posted. Panel-deposit 5420776111.

**All three refuted the issue's load-bearing claim, independently, by inventory.** I wrote that "Directive has no liveness signal from a dispatched child back to its orchestrator." That is false. I argued it from absence without surveying, which is exactly what the Stop 1 write-back flagged as the weak point — so the refutation landed where the triage predicted, just harder than I expected.

## What already exists

A child-to-parent liveness channel is shipped and documented. Long-running Cursor `Task` leaves are required to write `.deft-scratch/subagent-status/<agent-id>.json` (`docs/subagent-heartbeat.md`, and the preamble at `content/templates/agent-prompt-preamble.md:538-550`). The parent asks the question I claimed it could not ask, with `task agent:monitor` and `task verify:subagent-alive`. A stale or missing heartbeat prints `REDISPATCH_OK`, which is the existing takeover authorization. Swarm Phase 4 already names this the canonical alive-check.

The overnight cohort had **no `.deft-scratch/subagent-status/` directory at all** in any of the seven worktrees. Measured directly: `task verify:subagent-alive` against `b3721` exits **2** — configuration error, "scratch dir does not exist" — not **1** with `REDISPATCH_OK`. So the mechanism did not fail. It was never armed, by me, in the dispatch envelopes I wrote.

That reframes the issue entirely. It is not "no mechanism exists." It is "the shipped mechanism was not adopted, and here are the holes that remain even when it is."

## The finding I could not have reached

**The observer dies with the observed.** On this host the parent and its `Task` leaves are one workspace. A file heartbeat survives a bridge drop; a parent sitting on the same bridge cannot read it while the bridge is down. So the seven-hour silence is not evidence that no queryable signal can exist — it is operator re-entry latency. An always-on parent-to-child channel presumes a live parent, and this failure kills both ends together.

That splits the problem cleanly into two things I had conflated:

- **(a) in-flight observation**, valid while some process on that workspace is still up — already served by #1365 / #2824 when armed.
- **(b) morning-after operator visibility**, which must not require a live parent at all.

Nothing in my "Suggestions" section distinguishes these, and (b) is the half that actually cost seven hours.

## Three of my suggestions are refuted outright

**"A cohort manifest carrying per-child last-seen"** — rejected. The C2 launch manifest is static dispatch PREP and `swarm:launch` writes it with `mode: "replace"`. Measured: it currently holds a later `3596` cohort, not the overnight seven. Runtime last-seen on that file would be erased by the next launch, and it would mix allocation consent with liveness.

**"Worker death as a detectable state distinct from BLOCKED and DONE"** — rejected as a child-written event, for the obvious reason once stated: the child is dead and cannot write it. Heartbeats require a terminal write before exit, and a disconnect mid-tool cannot produce one. Worse, there is an existing contradiction to reconcile first — Phase 4 says treat a missing record as "alive but quiet" on one path, while `verify:subagent-alive` treats a missing *required* agent as dead, but only after the parent created the directory. Host-kill therefore looks identical to "never started." Adding a third classifier before reconciling the two that exist would make it worse.

**"Whatever the orchestrator holds for a child should expire"** — this one survives in spirit but not as a lease dimension. See scope below.

## A hole none of us had named

**The resume gate classifies a dead worker as a live peer.** Swarm pre-dispatch wires `DENY_DUPLICATE_ACTIVE` with `maxActiveAttempts: 1`, so a non-terminal attempt blocks a new spawn, and `completeAttempt` is caller-driven. Measured: **79 of 100 on-disk delivery-attempt ledgers are still `queued` or `running`, and none moved on 08-24 or 08-25.** So a killed worker sits `running` forever, and `REDISPATCH_OK` and `DENY_DUPLICATE_ACTIVE` then contradict each other until a human cancels. My issue said "no resume." The sharper truth is that resume is actively blocked by a stale non-terminal attempt, and any mortality design must name takeover as `swarm:pre-dispatch --action cancel` followed by begin.

And the counter-pressure is real: a death signal cheaper to fire than #2824's mkdir-plus-grace-plus-`--require-agent` re-opens the duplicate-writer failures (#261 / #263) on every workspace blip. Four clustered deaths make a batch re-dispatch especially tempting, which is precisely when two writers on one worktree is most likely. Who may declare a child dead, after what grace, and which of the three identities in play — occupancy `session_id`, heartbeat `agent_id`, ledger `workerId` — gets cancelled, has to be deterministic.

## Scope: this is not a #3613 lease dimension

My write-back asked whether "child mortality" belongs alongside liveness, lifecycle, and keyspace under #3613. The panel's answer is no, and the reasoning holds: #3613's shape is the worktree occupancy lease, which is a session signalling about **itself** — per-tree write exclusion, expire-to-free. Child mortality is a parent observing **another process**, a different primitive with a different keyspace, already owned by #1365. Keeping #3730 filed as a fourth lease dimension biases the next build toward putting last-seen in `occupancy.json`, which cannot produce a cohort roster and collides with both #3599 and #3729.

The causal link to #3604 is real — a killed worker skips `releaseOccupancy`, so every disconnect mints ghost leases. That makes this an **upstream producer of** #3604, not a member of the lease family. Re-file as related-to #3613 / #3604, and if it needs a tracker at all it belongs next to #1365 / #2824 / #3228 in swarm and host-adapter topology.

Not nothing, and worth stating so the recut does not throw it away:

Retitle and rescope from "Directive has no liveness signal" to something like *the shipped subagent-heartbeat path is unarmed by default and blind to host-kill*, with three separable pieces:

1. **Adoption.** Dispatch envelopes must arm the existing path — parent creates the scratch directory, worker is told to heartbeat, `--require-agent` is set. My own envelopes did none of this, which is the single most actionable line in the whole issue.
2. **Reconcile the two existing classifiers** before adding any third: Phase 4's "alive but quiet" versus `verify:subagent-alive`'s missing-required-agent-is-dead.
3. **Morning-after operator visibility that does not require a live parent** — the (b) half above. ## An eleventh instance, observed live tonight — and it corrects one of my own framings

Posting after the round-1 panel. This is new evidence, not a critic input.

At roughly 01:22 local on 2026-08-26 the workspace bridge dropped again and killed a `drive-to: merge-ready` worker mid-flight, with the same `turn_ended` / `Workspace Disconnected` signature. That is an eleventh worker death, in a cohort of three, on a night when nothing unusual was running.

Three things it shows that the filed incident did not.

### The residue is worse than "no resume" — it was zero commits

The killed worker was building #3753. State when I inspected it:

```
0 commits ahead of origin/master
10 dirty paths
```

Two brand-new source files totalling ~18 KB — a complete module and its test — plus seven modified files, none of it committed. Roughly an hour of work existing only as uncommitted worktree state.

My filed description says a killed worker's "unit of work is abandoned mid-flight." That understates it. The work is not merely unfinished, it is **unversioned**: nothing in git, nothing pushed, no PR, and no artifact any recovery gate could discover. `verify:orphan-active` cannot see it. The delivery-attempt ledger records the attempt as `running` forever. The only reason it survived is that the worktree directory persisted on disk and I happened to look.

### But it was fully recoverable, which supports the panel over my framing

I inspected the uncommitted diff, verified it implemented the recut contract rather than the refuted one, and re-dispatched a worker to commit and ship it rather than rebuild. Recovery cost was a few minutes of reading.

That is direct support for a panel disposition I had recorded but not evidenced: **resume-or-cancel at cohort re-entry is the right primitive, because a mid-flight worktree is usually recoverable.** It also supports the critic's argument that what is missing is not a new child-written death event — the child cannot write one, and this one certainly did not — but a **parent or operator inference from worktree state after the fact**.

Worth naming precisely: the recovery signal that worked was *uncommitted worktree state*, which is not a heartbeat, not a ledger entry, and not on the C2 manifest. None of the three surfaces the issue originally proposed would have found it.

### The same-bridge finding holds, and there is an interaction nobody has recorded

The panel's sharpest point was that the parent and its `Task` leaves share one workspace bridge, so the observer dies with the observed, and the original seven-hour silence was operator re-entry latency rather than missing signal.

Tonight the parent survived and the child did not, so detection was immediate — consistent with that model.

But re-dispatch was then **blocked** by something outside the issue's frame. The session ritual had aged past its four-hour staleness window during the run, so the spawn gate denied the recovery dispatch until I ran `session:start --rearm`. So on a long cohort, the ritual clock can expire *while workers are still running*, and the first thing a parent tries to do after a disconnect — re-dispatch — is exactly what the stale ritual refuses.

That composes badly with the twelve-to-one lifetime mismatch recorded on #3729: a four-hour ritual window and a twenty-minute lease window are both shorter than a real cohort, and both failures surface at recovery time rather than during normal operation.

Re-arming also reclaimed the occupancy lease, which immediately blocked my own direct writes under #3611 until I released it — so the recovery path for a dead child currently walks straight through two other open defects in this cluster.

### What I am not claiming

I have not established the cause of this drop, and I am not asserting it shares a cause with the four clusters in the filed incident. No vendor incident was checked for tonight's window. The count of eleven is deaths observed, not a claim about a single mechanism.

### Disposition

No change to the round-1 disposition map or to the accepted findings. This strengthens two already-accepted items — resume-or-cancel, and parent-side inference over child-written death — and adds one item for the recut that no critic raised:

**The recovery path must survive a stale ritual.** A parent that detects a dead child and tries to re-dispatch will be denied by the gated ritual if the cohort has run longer than the staleness window. Either the recovery dispatch re-arms as part of its own flow, or the operator gets a message naming `session:start --rearm` instead of a bare denial.

## Recut applied — and why the chip stays `mechanism-shaped`

The body is recut against the round-1 disposition map and retitled. The withdrawn framing, the three rejected suggestions, and the #3613 re-scoping are all now in the body rather than only in the lean.

The chip stays at `design-critique:mechanism-shaped` deliberately, and I want to record why rather than let it look like an oversight.

The disposition map was total and all-accept, so the critique itself is complete. But five of the six acceptance items are ordinary engineering and **one is not**:

| Item | State |
|---|---|
| 1. Arm the shipped path in dispatch envelopes | designed, small, independent |
| 2. Reconcile the two existing classifiers | designed, needs a decision between two shipped behaviours |
| 3. Terminal state for a killed worker's attempt | designed, unblocks resume |
| 4. **Operator re-entry visibility without a live parent** | **no design at all** |
| 5. Recovery survives a stale ritual | designed, small |
| 6. Envelopes instruct workers to commit early | designed, trivial |

Item 4 is the genuinely unserved need this issue exists for, and it is the one thing no critic proposed a mechanism for. The constraints on it are unusually tight: it cannot sit on the C2 launch manifest (overwritten per launch, measured), it cannot sit on `occupancy.json` (per-tree write exclusion, expire-to-free, session-self), it cannot depend on the child having written anything (the child is dead mid-tool), and it cannot depend on a live parent (the observer dies with the observed on the same bridge). It also must not be cheaper to fire than the existing takeover authorization, or it re-opens #261 / #263 on every blip.

Stamping the whole issue `triage-ready` would imply a worker could pick it up and build it. Items 1, 3, 5, and 6 are genuinely that. Item 4 is a design problem wearing an acceptance checkbox.

**Recommendation for the operator: split.** Items 1, 3, 5, 6 into an "arm and unblock the shipped path" issue that is immediately buildable; item 2 as a small decision issue; item 4 as its own design-critique arc, since an open solution space with a high blast radius is exactly the panel condition. I have not split it — the recut changed enough already, and the split is a judgement about how to carve work rather than a critique outcome.

## Filed relationship change, not yet applied

The body now records this as **related to** #3613 rather than a fourth lease dimension, and as an **upstream producer of** #3604. The actual re-parenting on #3613's current-shape comment has not been done — #3613 belongs to a cluster the operator asked me to work but whose tracker comment I have not edited, and moving a child out of an umbrella is the kind of edit that should be visible rather than incidental.
